title: Microburst Orchestration Pilot Check-in
summary: Weekly sync focused on microburst mitigation and first-token/streaming latency. Reviewed recent benchmark runs, kernel path choices, and a proposed hedging policy. Customer asked for SOC2/KMS details and a compact pricing sketch for Dedicated pilot. Agreed on two experiments and a follow-up demo next week.
next_steps: Redwood to share trimmed benchmark CSV and quick pricing sketch for 2-week Dedicated pilot
Customer to run internal trace with new short-prefix dataset and share results by Tue
Schedule kernel A/B demo with logs enabled next Wed
action_items: Liam Patel - produce trimmed benchmark CSV and notes - due 2026-04-06
Rajesh Iyer - run short-prefix trace and upload to shared drive - due 2026-04-07
Maya Chen - send Dedicated pilot pricing outline and SOC2 pointer - due 2026-04-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03 10:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ana (Redwood CSM), Rajesh (Cobalt ML), Sofia (Infra), Tom (Arch)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Rajesh: yeah, loud and clear. thanks. happy friday.
[00:12] Liam: awesome, quick agenda, we'll run through the latest microburst bench, highlight TTFT numbers, then kernel path decisions and proposed hedging policy, then security questions and next steps.
[00:24] Tom: sounds good. we're mostly interested in first-token variance and whether early-path helps for our microburst tail.
[00:32] Sophia: and also cost impact - we need to justify Dedicated briefly.
[00:36] Maya: got it. quick sanity check: you exported the traces we asked for last week?
[00:42] Rajesh: yes, we pushed a sample short-prefix trace to the shared folder, it's about 600 sessions, mix of seq len 16-512. note there was some noise from our front-end batching.
[00:55] Liam: thanks, we'll use that to correlate KV cache hit rates. ok slide 1 — run summary.
[01:02] Liam: in the last run we measured median TTFT 48ms on the streaming hedged path and 86ms on the conservative kernel path, p95 at 210ms on conservative, p95 120ms on hedge. note: numbers include network in our hosted lab — your infra numbers may differ.
[01:25] Rajesh: 48ms median is promising, but p95 120 is still high for 95th percentile. what's the microburst behavior? are there repeated spikes or single-burst ones?
[01:37] Liam: mostly microbursts — short burst of concurrent requests that overwhelm per-GPU queues briefly. hedging to a lighter kernel with early token path helps reduce TTFT variance but increases token CPU usage slightly.
[01:50] Ana: small note — the hedging policy also enables automatic fallback to quantized variants when queueing crosses threshold.
[01:59] Sofia: how deterministic is kernel selection? we worry about jitter when the selector oscillates.
[02:04] Liam: good question. our selector uses a stabilized hysteresis window, plus count smoothing over 30s. we've seen oscillation only when load crosses close to threshold rapidly; the hedging policy includes a short cool-down to prevent thrash.
[02:20] Tom: that cooling sounds useful. can we tune it per deployment?
[02:24] Maya: yes, it's configurable in the rollout policy; for Dedicated pilot we can pre-set a conservative cool-down.
[02:30] [02:30] Rajesh: I wanted to call out sequence length distribution - our logs show 70% seq <=64, but 10% of requests are 256-512 and they cause the biggest tails.
[02:42] Liam: right — the heavy tail of long sequences leads to KV-cache churn and kernel path re-evaluation. two levers: 1) early-response path for seq <=64, 2) isolated path allocation for long-seq heavy requests (route to reserved workers). each has cost tradeoffs.
[03:00] Maya: can you quantify the reserved workers cost?
[03:03] Liam: rough ballpark: reserving one small GPU worker pool for long-seq (~20% capacity) increases monthly bill by ~12-15% but cuts p95 for the short-route by ~30-40%. numbers depend on your QPS.
[03:15] Sofia: that could be acceptable if p95 improves. our SLO is 200ms p95 for interactive flows.
[03:22] Rajesh: also curious about quantization — you mentioned quant-decisions in Optimize. does quant cause quality regressions for our prompts?
[03:30] Liam: we've got model-specific quant profiles; for your eval set quant-8 post-distillation had a small BLEU-style drop in one prompt, but most prompts were fine. idea is to do a canary with your key prompt set.
[03:45] Tom: can we run an A/B across 1% traffic? we'd like to see regression metrics before enabling on production.
[03:51] Maya: absolutely — canary is standard. we'll also tie regression alerts to your prompt tests in Redwood Console.
[03:58] [04:00] Rajesh: on security, Sofia flagged KMS and audit logs — do you support customer-managed keys and fine-grained audit exports?
[04:09] Ana: yes, for Dedicated we support CMK integration and audit log streaming to your SIEM, plus SSO/SAML and role-based access. SOC2 attestation is available — I'll drop the pointer in chat.
[04:21] Sofia: good — also need data residency for EU region soon, can your private deployment be region-locked?
[04:28] Maya: yes there are Private options, and Dedicated can be region pinned. we'll include region notes in the pricing doc.
[04:36] Rajesh: back to latency - you said hedging increases token usage. by how much?
[04:41] Liam: in our bench, hedging increased token compute by around 6-9% because some requests hit a lighter kernel then fall back and produce duplicate token work; but amortized cost per net useful token was up ~4%. depends on hit rates.
[04:56] Tom: any quick wins we can do on our side without Dedicated? maybe prompt engineering or client-side batching changes?
[05:02] Rajesh: we are already batching at 30ms windows, maybe reduce to 20ms for interactive endpoints? but that could increase QPS and microbursts.
[05:12] Liam: alternatively, prefix caching helps a lot when you have repeated system prompts or identical prefixes — that seems applicable given your 70% short sequences. we saw a 20-25% TTFT uplift when prefix caching hit rates exceed ~40%.
[05:28] Rajesh: we have a lot of repeated system text — plausible. we'll instrument cache keys.
[05:33] [06:00] Maya: demo-time: Liam, can you show the hedging behavior in the lab replay?
[06:05] Liam: sure, pulling up the replay. bear with me, replay simulates a 400 QPS spike.
[06:15] [screen share noise omitted]
[06:22] Liam: okay here the conservative kernel queue fills, you can see request latency climb to 300ms, then hedging routes some to the early path and TTFT drops to 65ms for those requests.
[06:35] Rajesh: I see in the logs some misattributed model names like "Redfield-lite" — are those internal labels?
[06:41] Liam: yeah the transcriber sometimes mangles names, it's actually "Redwood-lite-quant".
[06:45] Sofia: noted. are logs fine-grained enough to reconstruct per-request kernel decision and KV-cache status? we need that for postmortems.
[06:54] Liam: yes, we emit a brief decision trace per request: timestamp, selected kernel, cache hit/miss, queue depth. we'll include a sample trace in the CSV.
[07:05] Tom: how big are those traces? any PII concerns?
[07:10] Ana: traces are metadata-only, no user text by default; you can enable payload capture behind a policy if you consent.
[07:18] Rajesh: good. on the pilot duration, we'd prefer a 2-week Dedicated window to run stress tests — is that feasible?
[07:26] Maya: yes, we can provision a 2-week Dedicated pilot with guarded SLA; cost sketch will go in doc.
[07:32] [07:45] Sofia: one more on orchestration — if the selector fails or misroutes under heavy load, can we auto-fail to a single stable path?
[07:52] Liam: we have a fallback route policy that will pin to the conservative kernel for a short interval if error rates climb. it's part of the graceful degradation flow.
[08:02] Rajesh: what's the typical error rate delta between paths? edge kernel tends to drop precision occasionally?
[08:09] Liam: not really error rates, more about slight output divergence under heavy quant. For early-response kernels we control sampling temperature and output length to preserve semantics. we'll show divergence metrics in A/B canary.
[08:25] Maya: quick poll — are we aligned to run the two experiments: 1) short-prefix canary with prefix cache enabled, 2) hedging on streaming path with a reserved worker pool for long seq?
[08:36] Rajesh: yes.
[08:37] Tom: yes.
[08:38] Sofia: yes, pending the price outline.
[08:40] Maya: great. I'll send the outline, Liam will share bench CSV.
[08:45] [09:00] Rajesh: side question — any known incompat with our telemetry stack? we use Fluentd -> Splunk pipeline.
[09:07] Ana: we can stream logs to S3 and you can pick them up, or use direct delivery to Splunk via syslog. we've done Fluentd integrations before.
[09:17] Sofia: ok that'll work.
[09:20] [09:30] Liam: quick note on test metrics — we'll include TTFT median/p95/p99 and queue depth percentiles plus cache hit rate.
[09:37] Rajesh: please include per-kernel token counts.
[09:41] Liam: will do.
[09:44] [10:00] Tom: any blockers on your side?
[10:03] Maya: none from Redwood — we're just waiting on your short-prefix trace results and confirmation to spin up the Dedicated pilot.
[10:10] Rajesh: we'll try to run the trace by Tuesday and confirm pilot by Wed EOD.
[10:14] Maya: perfect. I'll follow up with meeting notes and the pricing + SOC2 links.
[10:19] [10:30] Sofia: quick nit — can we get the bench CSV with anonymized request ids?
[10:25] Liam: yes we'll scrub PII, only include hashed ids.
[10:30] [10:40] Maya: ok let's wrap. recap and owners: 1) bench CSV (Liam), 2) pricing/SOC2 (Maya), 3) internal trace (Rajesh).
[10:50] Rajesh: thanks all. appreciate the focused demo.
[10:54] Tom: thanks, talk soon.
[11:00] End.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and abbreviated labels; treat numeric numbers as approximate lab values.
